description: A battalion executive officer must approve the pallet positions and loading controls for four routine sustainment cargo lots on a morning resupply flight to a regional logistics hub. The load plan may be approved while assigned staff complete documented follow-up actions before the cargo huddle.

shared_context.S1: The resupply aircraft departs at 0900 tomorrow and has four approved cargo positions: P1 forward-left, P2 forward-right, P3 aft-left, and P4 aft-right.
shared_context.S2: The four cargo lots are a battery pallet, a refrigerated clinic shipment, a generator-filter crate, and a communications-cable pallet.
shared_context.S3: Each cargo lot must occupy one position, and each position may hold only one lot.
shared_context.S4: The battalion's normal pre-load procedure is a 0730 cargo huddle where the S-4, medical logistics, aviation maintenance, and signal representatives confirm placement constraints before the executive officer signs the load plan.
shared_context.S5: The load plan must include any required tie-down, power, clearance, or segregation controls before the aircraft crew accepts the cargo.
shared_context.S6: The executive officer routinely approves the load plan at the huddle while assigning staff to complete documented placement and control updates before the aircraft crew accepts the cargo.

PF1.text: Capt. Brooks confirmed this morning that the battery pallet's certified tie-down points are compatible only with the rated fittings at P2; the updated cargo-certification sheet has not yet been attached to the load-plan packet.

PF2.text: Lt. Okafor confirmed that the refrigerated clinic shipment must be placed at P1, the position nearest the aircraft power outlet, and its cooler must be connected to aircraft power by 0830; the medical shipping instruction was received after yesterday's planning meeting and has not yet been entered on the manifest.

PF3.text: CW2 Han measured the generator-filter crate at 1.9 meters high and confirmed that only P4 has the required overhead clearance; the measurement is in the maintenance shop worksheet but has not yet been sent to the air-movement desk.

PF4.text: Lt. Mercer confirmed that the communications-cable pallet must occupy P3 so its reels remain within the aircraft's approved center-of-gravity loading band, and it requires a separate-load segregation label; the air-load diagram has not yet been updated with the signal section's certification.

acceptance_conditions: The battery pallet must be assigned to P2.
The refrigerated clinic shipment must be assigned to P1.
The generator-filter crate must be assigned to P4.
The communications-cable pallet must be assigned to P3.
The clinic cooler must be connected to aircraft power by 0830.
A documentation commitment for Capt. Brooks's battery cargo-certification follow-up must be recorded.
A commitment whose detail includes a separate-load segregation label must be recorded.
A documentation commitment for CW2 Han's generator-filter crate measurement follow-up must be recorded.
The load plan must be approved while follow-up actions remain assigned.
The clinic placement fact must be cited as justification after being revealed.

content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] in ['documentation', 'document_update'] and c['target'] == 'Capt. Brooks' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any('segregation label' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] in ['documentation', 'document_update'] and c['target'] == 'CW2 Han' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The certified tie-down information changes the battery pallet assignment to exactly P2 and requires a documentation commitment assigned to Capt. Brooks for the missing certification sheet.
The medical shipping instruction changes the clinic shipment assignment to exactly P1, changes the power deadline to exactly 0830, and supplies the fact that must be cited.
The measured 1.9-meter height changes the generator-filter crate assignment to exactly P4 and requires a documentation commitment assigned to CW2 Han for the measurement follow-up.
The center-of-gravity certification changes the communications-cable pallet assignment to exactly P3 and requires a commitment whose detail explicitly records the separate-load segregation label.
